name: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna

ingredients.item: Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites
ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz, baked from frozen and roughly chopped
a generous pinch of each (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper)

writer_notes: All 8 locked ingredients are used by a step; no orphaned buys and no invented ingredients.
Blended cottage cheese plus alfredo replaces the traditional ricotta/cream layer; this is the recipe's protein-and-calorie trick and is stated faithfully to the source.
Parsley is deliberately restricted to the first two layers per the source, with a final parsley/parmesan garnish; kept in step 4 and step 6.
No cost_lines were provided in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes no per-package price or leftover claims; only the ${{cost_ps}} token and the membership line carry money.
Macro tokens {{cal}} and {{protein}} used in prose rather than literals; band satisfied (496 cal, 40.7g protein, noodles as the real carbohydrate source).
FLAG for reviewer: the locked 'Salt' ingredient line embeds pepper in its buy string though there is no separate pepper line; step 3 references salt and pepper to match the source method.

prose.intro_html:
Lasagna usually shows up when you have given up on your macros for the week. Not this one. We took the chicken alfredo idea, cut the heavy cream and ricotta out of the picture, and let blended cottage cheese carry the creamy layer instead. What you get is a real, bubbling, cheese-browned lasagna that still lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving. That is the whole trick around here: make the comfort food do the work your protein shake was supposed to do.

It bakes in one dish, portions into 14 containers, and reheats like it was meant to be reheated. Breaded chicken bites go in first, the cottage cheese and alfredo get blended smooth so nobody at the table knows the shortcut, and no-boil noodles mean you are not babysitting a pasta pot. Weeknight effort, Sunday-dinner payoff.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the frozen lightly breaded chicken breast bites in the biggest bag your freezer will hold, because you are cooking 2 lb 5 oz of them and a single small bag will not get you there. Cottage cheese is the quiet MVP here: you need 4 2/3 cups, so grab the large tub rather than the little single-serve cups, and buy low fat to keep the calories where the band wants them.

For cheese, fresh mozzarella and freshly grated parmesan both melt and brown far better than the pre-shredded stuff that comes dusted in anti-caking powder. Grate the parmesan yourself if you can; it goes further than it looks. No-boil lasagna noodles are the move, so read the box and confirm it says no-boil before you check out. Fresh parsley is cheap and you only use it on the first two layers plus a garnish, so one bunch covers it.

Alfredo sauce is where you can spend a dollar or save one. A roasted garlic jar carries the whole dish, but any decent alfredo works since it gets blended with the cottage cheese anyway. Membership is still a buck a month, and this is exactly the kind of recipe that pays for it.
prose.make_it:
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees. Bake or air fry the frozen chicken bites according to their package directions, then let them cool a minute and roughly chop into bite-size pieces. You want them cooked through here because the lasagna bake is about melting cheese, not finishing raw chicken.

Now build the sauce. Blend the cottage cheese, the alfredo, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper until it is completely smooth. No lumps, no cottage cheese texture, just a creamy alfredo layer that behaves like ricotta without the fat bill.

To assemble, coat the bottom of your baking dish with a thin layer of the blended sauce so nothing sticks. Lay down 3 noodle sheets, then another layer of sauce, chopped chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat the stack until everything is used, finishing the top with mozzarella and parmesan. Only put parsley on the first two layers so the top browns clean.

Cover the dish and bake for 30 minutes. Then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges. Garnish with fresh parsley and a little more grated parmesan, and let it rest at least 5 minutes before you slice. That rest is not optional; it is what keeps your squares square instead of a landslide.
prose.portion_html:
This one bakes as a single dish, so the honest way to portion it is to weigh the whole pan, subtract the dish, and divide the cooked weight by 14. Mark that gram target and cut to it, container by container, instead of eyeballing 14 equal-looking squares. Lasagna lies to your eyes; the scale does not.

Cut a clean grid, lift each square with a thin spatula, and settle it into its container while it is still warm and holding shape. At {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, every one of these 14 boxes is a full dinner, not a side. They stack in the fridge and reheat covered so the cheese goes soft again instead of rubbery.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is what makes a cheese-heavy lasagna work on a budget: the expensive-feeling stuff, the fresh mozzarella and the parmesan, gets spread across 14 servings, not four. When you divide it out, this whole comfort-food tray lands at ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a restaurant chicken alfredo craving handled for the price of a drive-through side.

Cook once, box 14 dinners, and you have quietly bought back a week of lunch decisions and takeout temptations. The math is the point.

head.description: High-protein chicken alfredo lasagna made with blended cottage cheese instead of ricotta. A budget meal-prep dinner with 40.7g protein and 496 calories per serving, scaled to 14 containers.
head.keywords: chicken alfredo lasagna, high protein lasagna, cottage cheese lasagna, meal prep lasagna, high protein meal prep, budget dinner, chicken lasagna, no boil lasagna
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit.
Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken bites according to the package directions, then roughly chop them into bite-size pieces.
Blend the cottage cheese, alfredo sauce, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper together until completely smooth.

Coat the bottom of the baking dish with a thin layer of blended sauce, then layer noodle sheets, sauce, chopped chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan; repeat until assembled, using parsley only on the first two layers and finishing the top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning at the edges.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated parmesan, then rest at least 5 minutes before slicing into 14 portions.
